parts.context: A tour leader explains the schedule and rules for a walking tour of an old town.

transcript.text: G'day, everyone, and welcome to the Old Town Walking Tour. My name's Tom, and I'll be your guide for the next three hours. Before we set off, let me explain the plan for the day and a few ground rules.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: I should also say that this is a small group, so if you have questions during the walk, just ask. I would rather answer them on the spot than at the end.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: We have a lot to see, but it's not a race. The tour covers about four kilometres, mostly on flat ground, but some of the streets are cobbled, so I hope you're all wearing comfortable shoes.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: We start here at the fountain, in front of the town hall, at nine thirty. The first stop is the cathedral. We'll go inside for twenty minutes, and a priest has kindly agreed to explain the history of the windows.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: At ten thirty we leave the cathedral and walk along the river to the Merchants' Bridge. The bridge dates from the fourteenth century, and it's lined with tiny shops, where you can buy handmade paper and jewellery.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: Then at eleven fifteen we stop at the covered market for a break. There's a good bakery, and I recommend the cheese pastry, which is a local speciality. You'll have forty minutes there, so you can have a proper snack.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: After the market, at twelve o'clock, we climb the Clock Tower. There are two hundred and ten steps, but it's worth the effort, because the view from the top is the best in the town. If you don't want to climb, you can wait in the square with a coffee.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: At one o'clock, the tour finishes at the old castle, where we'll visit the museum. The ticket is included in the price, so you don't have to pay anything extra.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: Now, some important points. If you get lost, don't panic. Take a photo of the nearest street sign and call me. My number is on the card I'm about to give you, and I'll always answer.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: Please stay on the pavement near the traffic, as the old streets are narrow and the drivers are not always careful. Also, be aware of pickpockets near the market. Keep your bags closed and in front of you.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: Photography is welcome almost everywhere, but not inside the museum, and please ask before photographing local people. Most are friendly, but some find it uncomfortable.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: The weather forecast looks good, though it can change quickly here. I have a few spare umbrellas, which I can lend, but they usually disappear very fast.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: For anyone interested, I also run an evening tour of the same area on Fridays, where we visit three historic taverns. It costs extra, but includes a meal. Ask me at the end if you'd like to book.
transcript.speaker: TOM

transcript.text: Right, is everybody ready? Let's go. Our first stop is just around the corner.
transcript.speaker: TOM
